thread:
Jamie (Support): Customer reported duplicate external actions and duplicate billing when using tool-calls via our API. They say a single user action resulted in two outbound tool calls and two charges. Attaching logs and repro steps they shared. Escalating for triage. :warning:

Kevin (Eng): Can you paste the exact request payload and headers they used? curious about idempotency keys and whether retries were client or server side. :eyes:

Jamie (Support): Pasting the minimal repro they sent (they redacted user data):

```
POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "gpt-tool-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"create_invoice for order 12345"}],
  "tools": [{"name":"billing.create_invoice","schema":{"type":"object","required":["order_id"]}}]
}
```

Jamie (Support): They said client saw a 502 after 1st attempt, client retried automatically (sdk v0.9.2 with default retry policy), then got 200 and saw the invoice created twice. Their logs include our request_id: rq_0a9f3b. Extract from our logs: 

```
[2026-02-12T15:02:10Z] rq_0a9f3b tool_call.start tool=billing.create_invoice args={"order_id":12345}
[2026-02-12T15:02:10Z] rq_0a9f3b tool_call.error SchemaValidationError missing field "location"
[2026-02-12T15:02:11Z] rq_0a9f3b gateway 502 upstream read timeout
[2026-02-12T15:02:12Z] rq_0a9f3b tool_call.start tool=billing.create_invoice args={"order_id":12345}
[2026-02-12T15:02:12Z] rq_0a9f3b tool_call.success provider_resp={"invoice_id":"inv_873"}
```

Jamie (Support): Note first tool_call.error is a schema validation error from our tool call marshaller (missing optional "location" field). Seems odd: schema error then upstream 502 then retry succeeded — possible race between validation and network error handling. Customer claims they were charged twice.

Sunita (ML): Hm. Two possibilities: (1) Our runtime retried the entire chat request after the 502 (leading to a second tool invocation), or (2) the client retried and the SDK sent the request twice. Which retry layer shows the second attempt?

Owen (SRE): From logs above, both tool_call.start share same request_id (rq_0a9f3b) — that suggests the retry happened inside our gateway/runtime rather than a new client-origin request (clients normally get a new request_id). Can you run a trace on rq_0a9f3b to see where the 502 originated?

Kevin (Eng): Also check whether our gateway's retry policy treats SchemaValidationError as transient. It shouldn't. Schema errors are 4xx-equivalent — never retry. If the runtime treats it as transient because of how marshaller surfaces errors, we might be incorrectly triggering a retry.

Jamie (Support): Trace attached (shortened):

```
gateway -> runtime.marshaller -> runtime.tool-proxy -> upstream(billing-provider)
runtime.marshaller returned SchemaValidationError -> gateway observed an upstream read timeout 502 -> gateway retried request per policy (max_attempts=2) -> runtime re-invoked tool with same request_id
```

Jamie (Support): Customer also shared SDK logs showing the client only sent one request and never retried (sdk v0.9.2 had retries disabled by default in their config).

BillingBot: Detected two billing events for external provider for order 12345 from provider: billing-provider, timestamps 15:02:12Z and 15:02:13Z. Flagging for refund follow-up.

Owen (SRE): Quick hypothesis: marshaller raised a schema error, but the error bubbled up as a 502 to the gateway (bad mapping). Gateway interprets 502 as eligible for retry. That triggers a second tool invocation with identical args. If the provider is not idempotent, duplicate side-effects occur.

Sunita (ML): We also have our fallback behavior where if a tool-call errors we optionally fall back to a non-tool generation to continue the chat. Could that have triggered a second, different path that also invoked billing? (e.g., fallback attempted a different provider API)

Kevin (Eng): Two immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) Ensure SchemaValidationError maps to 4xx and is not retried by gateway. 2) Add server-side dedupe using an idempotency key derived from request_id or explicit header so tool providers see it. We should also add a short-term config flag to disable automatic retries for tool-calls.

Jamie (Support): Customer is asking for timeline and a refund. I told them we're investigating and asked for permission to refund if confirmed.

Owen (SRE): I'll cut a quick patch to gateway retry mapping: treat any marshaller/tool validation errors as client errors (no retry). Patch and roll out to PROD in next 30m as hotfix (will enable canary first).

Kevin (Eng): I'll add server-side idempotency header insertion in runtime.tool-proxy: if incoming request lacks X-Idempotency-Key, set X-Idempotency-Key=req_id. That should prevent provider-side duplicates for most cases. Also add a note to SDK docs recommending clients pass idempotency keys.

Sunita (ML): For the fallback -> non-tool path, add a guard: only run fallback simulation (non-tool) after ensuring tool failure was a true network transient. If failure is schema or 4xx, don't fallback to alternate provider. That avoids double-billing via alternate flows.

BillingBot: Action required: Issue refund workflow for provider charge duplicate. Suggest refund and credit to customer while we root cause. Filing ticket #BILL-4593.

Jamie (Support): Customer okay with refund. I'll log the ticket and request refund via BILL-4593. Also asked customer to confirm they didn't send any replays from their side (they confirmed no).

Kevin (Eng): Quick repro plan so we can validate fix: run a synthetic where marshaller rejects first call (simulate missing field error thrown as marshaller error), then have gateway return 502 to replicate prior mapping, and verify gateway does NOT retry after the hotfix. Also verify idempotency header present on tool proxy outbound.

Owen (SRE): I'll monitor error rate and tool-call counts for the next hour after hotfix. Rollout plan: canary 10% -> 100% in 10m if green.

Jamie (Support): I've told customer timeline: hotfix in 30m, idempotency rollout EOD, refund initiated. They want to be CC'd on billing ticket.

Sunita (ML): Follow-up: let's add an e2e test to our CI that simulates SchemaValidationError + gateway 502 to ensure no retry. Add a test case to prevent regressions.

Kevin (Eng): I'll own the runtime idempotency change (KEVIN-235). Owen will own retry mapping (OWEN-112). Jamie will own customer comms and billing ticket. Sunita will add CI tests.

Jamie (Support): Thanks all. Will update thread after the canary. :thumbsup:
